title: Noise-Aware Synthesis of Quantum LDPC Encoder Circuits via Two-Sided Hamming Descent
abstract: Quantum low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes are a promising route to fault-tolerant quantum computation, but their use requires efficient preparation of encoded states. Standard encoder constructions generate circuits through fixed algebraic procedures, yet the resulting circuit can contain substantial redundancy. We formulate LDPC encoder preparation as a circuit-resynthesis problem: given the linear-reversible matrix implemented by the encoder's CNOT block, we seek a lower-cost equivalent circuit that can be routed efficiently on the target hardware and which mitigates noise. We propose a novel optimization approach referred as two-sided Hamming descent and a noise-aware optimization pipeline for this task.   Across several families of Calderbank-Shor-Steane (CSS) LDPC encoders, including Bivariate Bicycle, hypergraph-product, and entanglement-assisted codes, the proposed pipeline produces substantially smaller and shallower encoder circuits than the standard constructions and the synthesis baselines considered, cutting gate counts by 53.8% in aggregate across the benchmark and by up to 68% on the Bivariate Bicycle family. The gains remain visible after routing, where the two-qubit depth is reduced by up to 71% and translate into higher-fidelity state preparation under circuit-level noise. On the Bivariate Bicycle family, live-range scheduling further reduces routed preparation failure by up to 13.7% without adding two-qubit gates to the selected circuit. These results indicate that encoder-matrix resynthesis, combined with hardware-calibrated selection and scheduling, is an effective compiler-level tool for preparing quantum LDPC code states.
summary: This paper presents a compiler-level tool to synthesize quantum circuits for preparing LDPC code states by treating it as an algebraic matrix resynthesis problem. The authors introduce 'two-sided Hamming descent' and integrate this with noise-aware scheduling, achieving substantial reductions in gate count and depth compared to existing methods. This work provides a blueprint for optimizing resource usage when implementing complex quantum error correction protocols on real hardware.
main_problem: The core problem is efficiently synthesizing low-cost, noise-mitigating quantum circuits required to prepare encoded states for Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check (LDPC) codes.
main_result: The proposed pipeline significantly reduces CNOT gate counts by up to 68% and two-qubit depth by up to 71% compared to standard constructions, leading to higher fidelity state preparation under noise.
method: It employs a novel optimization pipeline combining Two-sided Hamming Descent for circuit resynthesis with hardware-aware post-processing steps like commutation re-layering and live-range scheduling.
model_or_system: The system involves fault-tolerant quantum computation using CSS LDPC codes (e.g., Bivariate Bicycle). The task is to find a minimal CNOT circuit realizing the linear transformation matrix defined by the encoder's CNOT block.
key_observables: CNOT gate count, circuit depth (ASAP vs. commutation-aware), routed two-qubit depth, and preparation error under hardware noise.
important_parameters: The optimization involves tuning parameters like the idle-to-gate error ratio ($\kappa$) and assessing initial reset error ($p_{	ext{reset}}$).
main_assumptions: The method assumes that circuit redundancy can be removed via algebraic matrix reduction, and that hardware constraints (connectivity, idle time) significantly contribute to preparation error.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the six-stage noise-aware encoder pipeline; other figures demonstrate the realization of the same unitary matrix with different lengths, confirming the synthesis problem.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the problem by noting redundancy in standard constructions. It details the novel two-sided Hamming descent optimization, followed by integrating this into a full pipeline that includes commutation re-layering and noise-aware scheduling to achieve hardware-optimal circuits.
why_interesting: While focused on quantum error correction codes rather than AMO systems directly, the underlying principles of circuit synthesis, resource minimization (gates/depth), and noise modeling are highly relevant for designing control pulses or implementing complex gates in trapped ion or superconducting qubit architectures.
